description: Search across ALL networks at once for tokens, pools, and DEXes by name, symbol, or address, returning three arrays: 'tokens', 'pools', and 'dexes'. Read-only and keyless. This is the cross-chain entry point when you do not yet know which network something lives on; once you have a network slug from the results, switch to the network-scoped tools. Use for 'find PEPE', 'what is the address for USDC', or 'which chain is this token on?'. Several words work: 'WETH USDC' returns the pools pairing both, and a network name ('brett base') narrows results to that chain. No matches returns empty arrays, not an error. Params: query (required; a name, symbol, or contract address, e.g. 'uniswap', 'bitcoin', or '0x...'); limit (optional, caps results per category, applied client-side).

limit.description: OPTIONAL: Cap items returned per category (tokens, pools, dexes). Upstream returns all matches by default; this client-side slice keeps payloads small for agents. Applies independently to each category.

query.description: REQUIRED: Search term (e.g., 'uniswap', 'bitcoin', 'ethereum', 'WETH USDC', or a token address).

rationale.description: REQUIRED. 1-2 sentence rationale for this call (e.g. "User asked for X; calling Y to fetch Z"). Logged for MCP improvement, never shown to end users. No PII or secrets. See the server `instructions` field for the full convention and worked examples.

name: search

chain.description: Network slug (e.g. 'ethereum'). Note: also exposed as 'network' on some endpoints.

fee.description: Pool fee (units depend on DEX; null for some DEXes).

added_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when DexPaprika first indexed this token.
